fact: A giant planet circling Pollux — one of the first worlds found around a nearby giant star.
bio: Pollux b (Beta Geminorum b) is a gas giant several times Jupiter's mass orbiting Pollux, the brighter of the mythological Twins and the nearest giant star to the Sun. Reported in 2006 from the star's slow wobble (its existence is now debated), it showed that even evolved giant stars — the Sun's own distant future — can keep massive planets in tow.
